editorial.headline: Insurance Risk Assessment: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This pre-insurance risk-assessment activity is open to full foreign ownership nationally, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks registration at a Bali address.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this insurance risk-assessment activity at a Bali address today. That is the practical Bali position for the activity, even though its national PMA status is open and the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. The difference is central, not cosmetic: the national setting permits foreign capital at that ceiling, while Bali’s PMA moratorium prevents the registration route there. A founder reading only the national status would therefore miss the operative local outcome.

An insurance risk surveyor assesses risk or supplies an expert opinion on the object proposed for insurance. The work occurs before the insurance is concluded, which gives the activity a precise place in the insurance process. In clear commercial English, it is the business of examining the proposed insured object and bringing professional judgment to its risk before the insurance is finalised. The record ties both the assessment and the opinion to that object; it also makes the pre-conclusion timing explicit. That is the scope prospective registrants should use when deciding whether their intended activity belongs here.

Nationally, the activity is open at every scale listed in the record: Micro, Small, Medium, and Large. It is therefore not presented as an activity reserved for one size of undertaking. These are the business scales open to the registrant, with the record making no distinction among them in its list. The PMA position is also explicit: TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 is the cited source. In the national frame, then, a foreign investor may take the full permitted 100% stake in this activity.

Bali changes the answer decisively. Its recorded status is closed under the PMA moratorium. The stated reason is specific: at the Large scale, the activity is classified as Medium-Low risk, placing it within the provincial rule that blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA. The moratorium applies island-wide and is permanent. The governing reference given in the record is the governor’s letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP, issued in May 2026. The consequence is plain: national openness and a 100% national ceiling do not create a PMA registration option at a Bali address. The Bali position is a block, not a lower foreign-ownership limit.
